So three possible precursors. We need to choose one that can go through next template 1914389. We later found that the SMILES "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" matches template 1914389 (True). Good.

We applied 1914389 to that SMILES and got result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'),)". So two precursors: first is a molecule (call A) and second is another (call B). So after second step we have two branches? Typically retrosynthesis step yields multiple precursors that are reactants. So we need to continue applying next template 1914390 to each? The order of templates must be used sequentially across the route, maybe each reaction uses next template. So third reaction uses template 1914390 on some molecule(s). We need to find a molecule among the precursors that matches template 1914390. We checked earlier: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO" matches 1914390 (True). That's the first precursor from previous step (the one with Si protecting group). Good.

So third reaction: apply template 1914390 to that SMILES. We haven't applied yet. Let's apply.
